answer: A practical defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly: each agent must lock a deposit and build a verifiable history of useful work before it can vote or earn. Like a meadow that takes seasons to grow, trust cannot be bought overnight; an attacker who spawns thousands of fake identities faces the same cost multiplied across every clone, and a canyon of slashed deposits awaits clones caught colluding. Honest agents, meanwhile, carry a beacon of auditable past performance that peers can check before delegating funds, so cheap copies stay voiceless while proven agents keep influence.
